results.title: Inter-Annotator Agreement (IAA) | Datasaur
results.content: # Inter-Annotator Agreement (IAA). Data scientists have long used inter-annotator agreement (IAA) to measure how well multiple annotators can make the same annotation decision for a certain label category or class. We support two algorithms to calculate the agreement between two annotators. ✍ IAA is calculated in the background as soon as a project status changed to **Ready for review** (after all labelers mark the project as complete) or **Complete** (a reviewer marks the project as complete). * You can also filter the IAA for a specific project. * For this workspace level, IAA is calculated using a weighted average from all projects. This means it doesn't re-calculate the entire set of labels or answers from each project. Instead, the weighted approach considers the occurrence of each label or answer between two annotators, resulting in a more accurate calculation that represent the real situation. 2. * The IAA will also be available when you open the detail of a project.

results.title: Why inter‑annotator agreement is critical to best‑in‑class gen AI training
results.content: While traditional accuracy metrics once ruled annotation evaluation, **inter‑annotator agreement (IAA)** has become the centerpiece of quality assurance in generative AI workflows. IAA measures how consistently multiple annotators label the same content. For complex generative tasks (e.g., semantic similarity, reasoning), human IAA averages between **α = 0.68 – 0.76** across domains like accuracy, similarity or goal alignment, which closely matches LLM‑LLM agreement under controlled setups. 3. **Feedback Loops**: Used correctly, IAA becomes a continuous feedback mechanism — annotators meet, discuss disagreements, refine labels, and re‑calibrate guidelines mid‑project. 4. **Expert Credibility**: Expert annotators — versus crowdsourced raters — consistently show higher IAA in subjective tasks like coherence or style, reinforcing Sigma’s curated workforce advantage. IAA transforms disagreement from chaos into insight, serving as a compass for annotation quality and workflow design. IAA measures how consistently multiple annotators label the same content. * **Cohen’s κ**: Used for two annotators on categorical tasks, adjusting for chance agreement. * **Krippendorff’s α**: Handles multiple annotators, missing data, ordinal or free‑text labels. results.title: Inter-Annotator Agreement (IAA)
results.content: # Inter-Annotator Agreement (IAA). * Inter-annotator Agreement (IAA) is a statistical measure that quantifies the consistency among human annotators using metrics such as Cohen’s κ and Krippendorff’s α. Inter-annotator Agreement (IAA) is the fundamental statistical and methodological construct quantifying consistency among human annotators engaged in labeling, segmenting, or otherwise providing structured judgments over datasets. * Routine reporting of both **inter-** and **intra-annotator agreement**; intra-annotator agreement tracks label stability over time and isolates causes of low IAA due to subjective variance versus ambiguity or guideline inadequacy (Abercrombie et al., 2023). **Worker reliability weighting**: By leveraging inter-annotator and intra-annotator agreement, frameworks such as EffiARA compute annotator reliability scores used to re-weight samples during model training, directly improving downstream classifier performance—especially in low-agreement or subjective tasks (Cook et al., 2024). * **Multi-faceted reporting:** Combine intra-annotator agreement with IAA to dissect stability versus reliability and employ diagnostic matrices that distinguish subjectivity from ambiguity (Abercrombie et al., 2023). 4.
